The parts of a fitted regression

Source: R/racc.R
racc.Rd

The fits of ppmlfe(), ivfe(), ppmlcf(), expgmm(), fepnl(), gmmpnl(), didfe(), rdloc() and sarml() are lists, and the usual accessors read them: coef() gives the estimates by term, confint() their intervals, vcov() the covariance matrix of the estimates and nobs() the rows the fit used.

Arguments

object

A fit of one of the functions above.

...

Nothing; the generics of stats have it.

parm

NULL (every term) or the terms wanted: names of terms or their positions.

level

The level of the intervals: NULL (the fit's own; 0.95 for sarml()) or one number between 0 and 1. For every fit but that of sarml() it must be the fit's level.

Value

coef(): a named numeric vector, one estimate per term (per method for rdloc()). confint(): a matrix with a row per term and the columns lower and upper, with the level as the attribute "level". vcov(): a square matrix named by the terms. nobs(): one whole number.

Details

The intervals are those the fit computed, at the fit's own level (the bias-corrected interval of rdloc(), the bootstrap interval of ppmlcf()): they are read from the fit, not rebuilt from the standard errors, so confint() takes no other level; fit again with the level wanted. sarml() stores no interval, and its confint() is the normal one, estimate plus or minus the quantile times the standard error, at any level.

ppmlcf() (bootstrap) and rdloc() (one estimate by two methods) store no covariance matrix, so they have no vcov(). The matrix of sarml() has a row for rho and one for lambda whichever the model holds (NaN for the one it does not), as its help page says.

How a model is given

By the names of columns of data, or by vectors, each in the argument of its role: the outcome, the regressors, the instruments, the fixed effects, the clusters. There is no formula interface: a formula has no place for those roles, and the fixed effects are absorbed, not expanded into columns of a model matrix. Regressors are numeric columns; a column of labels is taken only as a fixed effect or a cluster. Missing and infinite values are refused, each in its own words, and no option drops them: the caller subsets first.

What a fit keeps

The terms keep the names of the input columns, in coef(), confint() and vcov(). Row names are not kept: a fit has one row per term, not per observation. Fitted values need the fixed effects, which are absorbed and never estimated, so the fits do not return them; fepnl() and gmmpnl() return their residuals (resid). Collinear regressors, and regressors the fixed effects absorb, stop the fit with a message that says so. A count fit that has not converged warns, and records it (conv, iter); tol and maxit set the stopping rule.

Speed

The time of a fit grows in proportion to the number of rows: ten times the rows take about ten times as long (measured for ivfe(), ppmlfe(), fepnl() and didfe() from a thousand to a hundred thousand rows).

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(u = rep(1:20, each = 6), x = rnorm(120))
d$y <- 1 + 0.5 * d$x + rnorm(120)
f <- ivfe(d, "y", x = "x", fe = "u")
coef(f)
#>         x 
#> 0.4803809 
confint(f)
#>       lower     upper
#> x 0.1880123 0.7727495
#> attr(,"level")
#> [1] 0.95
vcov(f)
#>            x
#> x 0.01951251
nobs(f)
#> [1] 120
